slot.brief: Find the equation of the line through the intersection of two given lines and a given point (or perpendicular to a given line), using the family L₁ + λL₂ = 0.

stem: The line through the intersection of $2x+y-3=0$ and $x-y-3=0$, perpendicular to $2x-3y+5=0$, is

verdicts.working: The intersection is (2,-1). The given line has slope 2/3, so the perpendicular slope is -3/2. Through (2,-1), the line is 3x+2y-4=0.

working:
$L_1=2x+y-3$, $L_2=x-y-3$ intersect at $(2,-1)$.
$L_1+\lambda L_2=0$ has slope $-\dfrac{2+\lambda}{1-\lambda}$.
The given line has slope $\dfrac{2}{3}$, so the required slope is $-\dfrac{3}{2}$.
$-\dfrac{2+\lambda}{1-\lambda}=-\dfrac{3}{2}\Rightarrow\lambda=-\dfrac{1}{5}$.
$5L_1-L_2=0\Rightarrow 9x+6y-12=0\Rightarrow 3x+2y-4=0$.

solution:
Solving the two equations gives their intersection $(2,-1)$. The given line has slope $\frac{2}{3}$, so the required perpendicular slope is $-\frac{3}{2}$.
$$y+1=-\frac{3}{2}(x-2)\quad\Rightarrow\quad 3x+2y-4=0$$
